notes: All metadata from Crossref REST API (api.crossref.org/works/<doi>) retrieved 2026-09-13; abstracts from Crossref/Europe PMC/OpenAlex.
bioRxiv full-text HTML via curl returned Cloudflare 'error code: 1015'; BSB full text was read through WebFetch summary only, so BSB method details are marked partial/unclear.

nature.com page for 10.1038/s41540-026-00767-3 served an accelerated-article preview containing only the abstract and recommendations; no methods/code-availability section was retrievable. Ruscone row rests on abstract plus repository README and PyPI metadata.

GitHub REST API rate limit hit mid-session; licenses of neuroelectro/neuroelectro_org, dtebaykin/InterLabEphysVar and marcorusc/mcp-biomodelling-servers (GitHub side) are unverified; the PyPI package license is from PyPI JSON.

rows.citation: De Schepper, R., Abi Akar, N., Hater, T., et al. (2022). Cross-comparison of state of the art neuromorphological simulators on modern CPUs and GPUs using the Brain Scaffold Builder. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: Morphologically detailed multicompartment cerebellar neuron and network models built with BSB and run in NEURON and Arbor
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares simulators and hardware configurations; no deliberate single-fault model alterations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - network benchmarks (small and large cerebellar networks) described; single-cell current-injection protocols not identifiable from the accessible text.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - cross-simulator output check reportedly uses population firing rates and raster plots; main metrics are time-to-solution and energy.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or test selection; benchmarking design only.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - performance benchmark, no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted edits or translations.
rows.software: arb-nrn-comp https://github.com/Helveg/arb-nrn-comp (GPL-3.0 per LICENSE file); Brain Scaffold Builder https://github.com/dbbs-lab/bsb (GPL-3.0 per GitHub API)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Treats simulator translation as a performance question with coarse output agreement; NeuroSem would test behaviour preservation of single-cell NeuroML models under recorded mutants and valid transformations with calibrated feature tolerances and a selected protocol battery.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; bioRxiv details API (v1 2022-03-04, CC BY-NC-ND, no published version listed); Semantic Scholar API; Europe PMC abstract (PPR464890); bioRxiv full text via WebFetch summary (curl blocked, error 1015); GitHub API + raw README/LICENSE
rows.found_via: Semantic Scholar API forward citations of LEMS 2014; Crossref-verified

rows.citation: Pauli, R., Weidel, P., Kunkel, S., et al. (2018). Reproducing Polychronization: A Guide to Maximizing the Reproducibility of Spiking Network Models. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 12, 46.
rows.model_type: Spiking network of Izhikevich point neurons (original C++/MATLAB code reimplemented in NEST)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - varies implementation choices one at a time (noise realization, integration resolution, analysis threshold, connectivity, plasticity); not a mutation-operator framework.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - a generalization section alters network stimulus; no current-clamp protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - network-level measures (polychronous group counts, rates, spectra), not single-cell electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of stimuli or tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - single worked reproduction case; guideline derived from it.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Documents that hidden implementation choices, including time step, change model conclusions in one network case; NeuroSem would systematize this for single-cell NeuroML models with recorded single-fault mutants, multi-protocol features, refinement-based tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; Europe PMC search (PMID 30123121, PMC6085985) abstract and full-text XML (methods/results/recommendations sections); OpenAlex abstract; GitHub API
rows.found_via: Europe PMC citations of OSB 2019 and ReScience; OpenCitations citations of OSB preprint

rows.citation: Tebaykin, D., Tripathy, S. J., Binnion, N., et al. (2018). Modeling sources of interlaboratory variability in electrophysiological properties of mammalian neurons. Journal of Neurophysiology, 119, 1329-1339.
rows.model_type: Statistical (random forest) meta-analysis of experimental metadata versus published rodent neuron electrophysiology (NeuroElectro); no mechanistic neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - observational curation of 509 articles; no controlled alterations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - uses reported summary values, not simulated or applied stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - curated features such as resting potential, input resistance, AP half-width, rheobase, AHP amplitude, max firing rate, adaptation ratio.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - selects explanatory metadata covariates, not stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - repeated 10-fold cross-validation and out-of-sample R2 for statistical models; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Concerns experimental-condition variability in measured data, useful background on feature sensitivity; NeuroSem addresses behavioural drift in computational models after transformations and would not reuse this method directly.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (vol 119, pp 1329-1339); Europe PMC metadata (PMID 29357465, PMC5966732); PMC full-text page pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5966732 (methods, code availability)
rows.found_via: Europe PMC citations of NeuroML 2010 and ModelDB 2004

rows.citation: Yang, P.-C., Jeng, M.-T., Lieu, D. K., et al. (2026). Large-scale synthetic data enable digital twins of human excitable cells. eLife, 15, RP110013.
rows.model_type: Cardiac ion-channel ODE (Kernik-Clancy iPSC-cardiomyocyte model, 52 parameters) with a deep neural network inverse model
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - broad parameter perturbations create synthetic cell populations for training; not single-fault mutants used to test detection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - composite voltage-clamp protocol built from many test potentials; one final protocol, voltage clamp rather than current clamp.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - network input is raw total-current trace; AP features (e.g. APD90, EAD incidence) analysed downstream, not a feature battery.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - iteratively adds the test potential giving lowest parameter-inference MSE, discarding less informative steps (forward selection).
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - 70:10:20 train/validation/test split of synthetic cells plus experimental recordings; no held-out model types or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - deep learning used for parameter inference, not for editing or translating models.
rows.software: Digital-Twin-for-the-Win https://github.com/ClancyLabUCD/Digital-Twin-for-the-Win-Personalized-Cardiac-Electrophysiology (GitHub license field NOASSERTION; archived on Software Heritage)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Optimizes a stimulus for parameter identifiability in one cardiac model; NeuroSem would select current-clamp protocols by coverage of detected behaviour-changing mutants across neuron models, with calibrated tolerances and held-out models and mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (incl. preprint and Software Heritage relations); Europe PMC (PMID 42489674, PMC13395456) abstract and full-text XML (results, methods: optimized protocol, data split); GitHub API
rows.found_via: Europe PMC lens search (perturbation / electrophysiological features)

rows.citation: Tewari, J., Dahl, B. W., Bates, B. A., et al. (2026). Benchmarking biochemical networks generated by large language models. eLife, 15, RP109709.
rows.model_type: Logic-based ODE signalling network models (Netflux) and core E. coli metabolic network models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares LLM-generated networks to curated references; no seeded single faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - scores predicted responses to many network perturbations and substrates; biochemical inputs, not electrical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - reaction recall, confusion matrices and perturbation-response accuracy.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - perturbation sets taken from prior validated models; no selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - references validated against independent experimental data; no discovery/held-out split for a method.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - three general-purpose LLM families generate models from gene lists, 10 replicates each, benchmarked structurally and behaviourally.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Benchmarks AI generation of systems-biology networks against ground truth; NeuroSem would target edits of existing neuron models, detecting silent electrophysiological drift with mutation-calibrated protocol batteries; its AI study is secondary and isolated.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; Europe PMC (PMID 42535653, PMC13427342) abstract and full-text XML (methods: prompting, replicates, Netflux conversion, data availability); GitHub API
rows.found_via: Europe PMC search (LLM AND NEURON simulator/NeuroML/biophysical neuron model/Hodgkin-Huxley) | Europe PMC LLM/AI agent + systems biology model generation; verified via Crossref + abstract

rows.citation: Ruscone, M., Vazquez, M., Valencia, A. (2026). Intelligent tool orchestration for rapid mechanistic model prototyping: MCP servers as AI-biology interfaces. npj Systems Biology and Applications.
rows.model_type: Multiscale cancer cell-fate model: signalling network (NeKo), stochastic Boolean (MaBoSS), multicellular agent-based (PhysiCell/PhysiBoSS)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no seeded faults described in abstract or README.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - single TNF-response use case; full text not retrievable (accelerated preview only).
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - single use case; portability tried across several LLMs.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLM agents build and configure models via MCP tool servers in natural language; systematic behavioural checking of outputs not described.
rows.software: mcp-biomodelling-servers https://github.com/marcorusc/mcp-biomodelling-servers ; PyPI https://pypi.org/project/mcp-biomodelling-servers/ (v2.3.0, MIT per PyPI metadata 2026-09-13)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides AI tooling for building models and notes the need for validation; NeuroSem would supply the behavioural regression evidence such AI-edited models lack, for neuron models specifically.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API; Europe PMC abstract (PMID 42297831); OpenAlex abstract/OA status; nature.com article HTML (abstract-only preview); GitHub search API and raw README; PyPI JSON API
rows.found_via: Europe PMC lens search (LLM AND computational model AND generation)
